name: Joule-class picosecond CPA with cryogenically cooled (77 K) Yb:YAG active-mirror amplifiers at 0.5-1 kW average power
plain_name: Amplify a kilowatt-class picosecond laser using crystals chilled by liquid nitrogen
description: Reagan et al. (Colorado State) amplify stretched pulses in Yb:YAG active mirrors cooled to 77 K by flowing cryogenic liquid; the 100-mJ stage sits on a cryogenic cooling manifold inside a vacuum chamber and the joule-level stage uses 30 mm x 30 mm x 2 mm composite active mirrors (1.5 J at 500 Hz; 1 J at 1 kHz).
keywords: Amplify a kilowatt-class picosecond laser using crystals chilled by liquid nitrogen

sources.citation: Scaling diode-pumped, high energy picosecond lasers to kilowatt average powers (Reagan et al., High Power Laser Sci. Eng. 6, e11, 2018, doi:10.1017/hpl.2018.3)

reported_equipment: cryogenic cooling manifold enclosed in a vacuum chamber

requirements.rationale: The active mirrors are cooled to 77 K, where Yb:YAG becomes four-level with higher cross-section and thermal conductivity.
The cryogenic cooling manifold carrying the gain medium is enclosed in a vacuum chamber.
Free-space pump and seed beams must reach the cooled active mirrors and exit after each pass, so the cold enclosure needs optical windows.
Joule-level active mirrors are 30 mm x 30 mm; the circumscribing diameter is 42.43 mm (rounded up to 42427 um).
Optional: the source cools the Yb:YAG disks with liquid nitrogen; a cryocooler with sufficient lift at 77 K could substitute.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
